newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to grant tax breaks for investors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to grant tax breaks for investors.

text.p: Bulgaria will grant tax preferences to investment projects worth over $5 million under a new bill approved by the cabinet on Thursday, Foreign Investment Agency director Ilian Vasilev said.
"The government approved a new Foreign Investment Bill providing tax preferences for investment projects considered by the local authorities as a priority," Vasilev told reporters.

Projects will be considered as priority if they are worth more than $5 million, or make effective use of local resources and create at least 200 jobs, or are implemented in regions with undeveloped infrastructure and high unemployment.
The government must rule individually in each case. If approved, investors would be freed from paying customs duties, fees and value added tax on machinery and raw materials, Vasilev said.
For the first 10 years, profit tax would be payable at half the regular rate. Foreign investors would be allowed to acquire rights over land and property, Vasilev said.
Bulgarian companies taking part in key projects with foreign investors could have their taxes waived or reduced.
Credits extended in the form of financial leasing, concession right contracts and management contracts would be treated as foreign investments, so profits can be repatriated.
Bulgaria had previously lifted a ban restricting repatriation of income generated by foreign investments of less that $50,000 in a bid to boost investment.
The Foreign Investment Law will be passed to parliament for debate in September after the summer recess.
Vasilev said proposals would be presented to the cabinet to increase minimum capital requirements for court registration of local legal entities as part of amendments to the Trade Law.
So far the minimum capital requirement for a limited liability company stood at 50,000 levs and for joint stock companies at one billion levs.
"The minumum capital requirement increase is an attempt to provide more liability to both domestic and foreign companies," Vasilev said. -- Sofia newsroom +359-2 981 4145
